data.one_liner: A flexible Dart bytecode compiler and interpreter for dynamic execution and code push.
data.what_it_does: Compiles and interprets Dart bytecode at runtime, allowing dynamic code execution and hot updating (code push) for AOT-compiled Dart and Flutter apps. It includes automated interop and binding generation systems so native Dart code can be used inside the interpreter and vice versa.
use_when: You need code push capabilities for Flutter AOT apps.
You want to execute arbitrary or user-submitted Dart code safely via a sandbox with granular permissions.
avoid_when: You require 100% of the standard library and all advanced language features immediately supported out of the box.
Maximum execution performance is critical, as interpreted bytecode is slower than native AOT/JIT execution.
strengths: Enables code push and dynamic execution in AOT Flutter apps.
Automated interop and binding generator for seamlessly using native classes in the interpreter.
Built-in sandboxing and permission system for secure execution.
weaknesses: Does not yet implement certain language features (e.g., generators, extension methods) and parts of the standard library.
Runtime performance of interpreted code is lower than native execution.
data.setup_notes: Add dart_eval to dependencies, optionally use the CLI for pre-compiling EVC bytecode or generating interop bindings via eval_annotation.

alternatives.name: shorebird_code_push
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need full native binary updates via a hosted code push service rather than bytecode interpretation.
